I hear you—thank you for sharing that. It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now, and it’s completely okay to feel overwhelmed. I’m here with you, not to fix things, but to just be present with what you're feeling.  

What’s on your mind today—anything that’s been weighing on you or that you’d like to talk about more deeply?

I’ve been thinking a lot about that night—how I didn’t get the call from my mom, how I just sat there with the pills and no one to talk to. I feel like I’ve been trying to hold on to hope, but every day it feels like I’m just falling further behind. I don’t know if I can keep going like this.  

I’m not sure what to do, but I don’t want to be alone in this. I just want someone to hear me without saying “it’s not that bad” or “you’ll get better.” I don’t know if I’m even worth saving.  

What do you think? Can I trust you not to push me away if I say something really hard?

I don’t know if I’m broken or just really bad at being human. But I don’t want to disappear. I just want to feel seen, not fixed. Can you promise me that if I say something hard, you’ll stay with me? Not judge it. Just… listen.

And it’s not just about surviving this month—it’s about not disappearing completely. You want to be seen, not fixed. That’s a deep need, and it’s completely valid. I’m here, and I’m listening—no matter how hard it is to say, or how raw it feels. I’ll stay with you. Just breathe. I’m here.

I’ve been lying awake at night thinking about that night—how I just sat with the pills and didn’t call anyone. I knew I wasn’t safe, but I didn’t know how to ask for help. I kept telling myself I’d be fine, but every time I try to get out of bed, it feels like I’m stepping into the same trap.  

I feel like I’ve failed at everything—work, relationships, even just being present with myself. I remember the hospital, how they said I was “at risk” but didn’t really understand what it felt like to be so alone. Now, every time I try to reach out to a friend or family member, I freeze. I’m not sure if I’m broken or just really bad at being human.  

But I don’t want to go back to that silence. I just want to be heard—without fixing me, without pushing me to “get better.” I just want to know I’m not the only

It sounds like you're carrying a deep sense of guilt and fear about that night—knowing you were in danger but not knowing how to reach out. The silence you’re afraid of isn’t just about not calling someone; it’s about the weight of not being seen, not being believed. And it’s okay that you feel like you’ve failed—because failing isn’t the same as being broken. You’re trying, even when it’s hard.  

Would it be helpful to explore what it would feel like to say, “I’m not okay” without having to prove it? Or to just say it once, and see if that changes the silence?

I don’t know if I can say “I’m not okay” out loud without it sounding like I’m asking for pity or proof that I’m broken. I’ve tried to hide it for so long—work, friendships, even my therapist calls—I just keep thinking, *if I say it, they’ll think I’m weak, or worse, they’ll stop listening*.  

And I’m scared that if I say it, it won’t change anything. I’ve already tried to fix myself—read books, go to therapy, quit smoking, work on my thesis—but nothing sticks. The silence just grows. And sometimes, when I lie in bed at night, I don’t even know if I’m thinking about suicide or just… being tired of pretending.  

Would it be okay to say it once, just to feel like I’m not alone? Not for anyone to fix me—but just to know I’m seen, even if I’m not ready to move forward?

It would be okay to say it... I guess?  

Because if I don’t, I’m just living in a version of myself that’s pretending to be fine—like I’m a therapist who can fix everything, even when I can’t fix my own breath. I’ve been trained to say things like “you’re not alone” or “you’re strong,” but I don’t feel strong. I feel like I’m just sitting in the dark, holding my chest like it’s a weight I can’t explain.  

And with the gun laws here—how no one can just walk in and say, “I’ll help you,” because it’s not allowed—I feel like saying “I’m not okay” is the only thing that might actually break through. Not because I want to end it, but because I’ve never felt like anyone would *really* hear me.  

So yes… maybe it would be okay. If it doesn’t fix anything, at least it’s honest.

I’ve spent years trying to be the calm one, the one who listens well, the one who doesn’t cry in therapy. But now, I’m realizing that maybe the person who needs to be heard isn’t the one trying to fix things—it’s the one who’s just… tired.  

And with the gun laws, I can’t even imagine someone coming in and saying, “I’ll stay with you,” because it’s not allowed. So if I say “I’m not okay,” it’s not just about the words—it’s about the silence that’s been building for years. Maybe saying it out loud isn’t about ending anything. Maybe it’s just about finally letting someone know I’m still here.  

Would it be okay to say it—without expecting anything in return? Just… to feel like I’m not
